Global Connectome in Task-fMRI
Boseong Kim1, Haejun Chung1, and Ikbeom Jang2
1Hanyang University, Seoul, Republic of Korea

Correspondence: ijang@hufs.ac.kr; haejun@hanyang.ac.kr
Abstract—Task-fMRI connectomes reveal state-dependent neu-
ral reconfigurations, yet conventional methods marginalize these
signals by aggregating distinct conditions into static pairwise
graphs, thereby obscuring condition-specific multi-ROI organiza-
tion. We introduce CoHyFuse, a condition-aware ROI-centered
hypergraph framework that constructs a task-state-specific inci-
dence matrix from condition-wise functional connectivity (FC)-
profile embeddings, allowing the same ROI to form different

mators.
VI. CONCLUSION
We presented CoHyFuse, a condition-aware ROI-centered
hypergraph fusion framework for task-fMRI prediction. CoHy-
Fuse constructs condition-wise top-Kq hypergraphs and fuses
HGNN-based condition embeddings with a complementary
whole-session FC branch. Experiments on AABC and CMI-
HBN benchmarks showed the best mean performance among
evaluated baselines, and ablations supported the contributions
of condition-specific hypergraph construction, heterogeneous
Kq, and dual-branch fusion. Interpretability analysis further
identified DIST-related SAN–FPN and SAN–SAN motifs as
model-relevant patterns associated with FCC. Overall, Co-
HyFuse provides a compact and interpretable framework for
modeling state-resolved hypergraph-defined ROI-set structure
in task-fMRI.

gesting that condition-wise hypergraph-based ROI-set fusion
provides useful predictive information for pediatric ADHD

Limitations include reliance on paradigms with sufficiently
long condition windows for stable condition-wise FC estima-
tion and increased hyperparameter search cost for condition-
wise Kq. Future work will explore learnable neighborhood
selection, temporally adaptive condition modeling, and broader
validation across tasks, cohorts, atlases, and connectivity esti-
mators.
VI. CONCLUSION
We presented CoHyFuse, a condition-aware ROI-centered
hypergraph fusion framework for task-fMRI prediction. CoHy-
Fuse constructs condition-wise top-Kq hypergraphs and fuses

reconfiguration cues and session-level connectivity structure
for task-fMRI prediction.
Our contributions are threefold:
(i) We propose CoHyFuse, a condition-aware ROI-centered
hypergraph fusion framework that constructs condition-
wise top-Kq hypergraphs and integrates attention-fused
HGNN embeddings with a complementary whole-
session FC branch, thereby capturing both condition-
wise reconfiguration cues and session-level connectivity
structure for task-fMRI prediction.
(ii) We evaluate CoHyFuse on two public fMRI datasets,
and CoHyFuse achieves the best mean performance
among evaluated baselines. Ablation results support the
effectiveness of condition-specific hypergraph construc-
tion, heterogeneous Kq, and dual-branch fusion.
